quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 RESULTS (CFO Chantelle Breithaupt): total revenues $2,490,000,000, up 28.9% year over year and above the upper end of the $2,300,000,000 to $2,400,000,000 guidance; gross margin 63.4% (above the 62% to 63% guide, down from 64.2% a year earlier on a higher mix of cloud and AI Titan sales); operating income $1,200,000,000 or 47.5% of revenue; net income $1,050,000,000 or 42% of revenue ('Arista delivering over $1,000,000,000 in net income for the first time'); diluted EPS $0.82, up 24.2%. International revenues $528,300,000 or 21.2% of total. Full year 2025 (CEO Jayshree Ullal): 28.6% growth to a record revenue of $9,000,000,000, non-GAAP gross margin 64.6% and non-GAAP operating margin 48.2%. CFO: fiscal 2025 diluted EPS $2.98 (+28.4%); Q4 cash from operations approximately $1,260,000,000; cash, equivalents and marketable securities approximately $10,740,000,000.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $2,490,000,000 (+28.9%); gross margin 63.4%; net income $1,050,000,000; EPS $0.82; FY2025 record revenue of $9,000,000,000 (28.6% growth)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 OUTLOOK RAISED (point-in-time; raised again on later calls): management raised the 2026 outlook to 25% revenue growth, 'delivering approximately $11,250,000,000', despite 'the mounting supply chain allocation, rising cost of memory, and silicon fabrication', in what the CEO called 'massive and a growing TAM of $100+ billion'. Gross margin range reiterated at 62% to 64% 'inclusive of mix and anticipated supply chain cost increases for memory and silicon'; operating margin outlook raised to approximately 46%; campus revenue goal of $1,250,000,000 maintained; AI centers goal raised from $2.75 to $3,250,000,000. Q1 2026 guide: revenues of approximately $2,600,000,000, gross margin between 62–63%, operating margin approximately 46%, tax rate approximately 21.5%. CEO Jayshree Ullal on why 25% is not cautious: the network lags customer CapEx (data centers, power and accelerators come first), much of the business is new products and AI use cases, and the guide reflects 'the reality of what we can ship, not what the demand might be'. She anticipates 'one, maybe even two additional 10% customers' in 2026, with the final share depending on acceptance criteria timing and the ability to ship amid supply chain allocation.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $11,250,000,000 (25% growth); gross margin 62% to 64%; operating margin approximately 46%; Q1 revenues of approximately $2,600,000,000

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 REVENUE MIX AND NEW CUSTOMER SEGMENTATION: by customer sector, cloud and AI titans 48%, enterprise and financials 32%, and AI and specialty providers 20% - a newly bifurcated category that 'now includes Apple, Oracle, and their initiatives, as well as emerging Neo Cloud'. CEO Jayshree Ullal said the category moved because of 'Oracle's AI, Acceleron, and multitenant partnerships', which give it a dual personality (some OCI, some fully AI-based). Cloud and AI titans are defined as customers with greater than a million servers, greater than 100,000 GPUs and an R&D focus on models and sometimes their own XPUs - 'less than five or about five'. By product line: core cloud, AI and data center (7000 Series on EOS) 65% of revenue, campus and routing adjacencies approximately 18%, subscription network software and services approximately 17%. Neo clouds split in two: healthy providers pivoting to AI that Arista will invest with, and a set 'we watch more carefully, because some of them are oil money converted into AI or crypto money converted into AI', where Arista checks the health of the customer.
quarterly_data.figure: cloud and AI titans 48%; enterprise and financials 32%; AI and specialty providers 20%; core 65% of revenue; adjacencies approximately 18%; software and services approximately 17%

quarterly_data.signal: MEMORY SHORTAGE AND PURCHASE COMMITMENTS: purchase commitments rose to $6,800,000,000 at year-end from $4,800,000,000 at the end of Q3, mostly chips for new products and AI deployments, with future variability from component pricing 'such as the supply constraint on DDR4 memory' and supplier lead times; inventory $2,250,000,000. CEO Jayshree Ullal: Arista absorbed much of the cost in 2025, but 'in 2026, the situation has worsened significantly' - memory prices are 'an order of magnitude exponentially higher', shortages are expected to 'lap multiple years', and 'memory is now the new gold for the AI and automotive sector'; she also expects increases from silicon fabrication because the chips are made 'essentially with one Taiwan Semiconductor'. Arista did not pre-buy all the memory it needs ('Chantelle's current commitments are not enough. We need more memory.') and expects 'a one-time increase on select especially memory-intensive SKUs'. Arista does not allocate among customers ('first in, first served'), but memory allocation could leave 'the demand is greater than our ability to supply'.

AI NETWORKING DOUBLING (point-in-time target): Arista exceeded its 2025 goal of $1,500,000,000 in AI center networking and is 'now doubling from 2025 to 2026 to $3,250,000,000 in AI networking revenue' (AI centers goal raised from $2.75 to $3,250,000,000). CEO Jayshree Ullal: three years ago Arista had no AI and InfiniBand was deployed everywhere in the back end; now 'we might do north of $3,000,000,000 this year and growing', a number that includes the front end tied to back-end GPU clusters in an all-Ethernet AI system. The rise of agentic AI 'will only increase not just the GPU, but all gradations of XPU that can be used in the back end and front end'.
quarterly_data.figure: $1,500,000,000 AI center networking goal exceeded (2025); $3,250,000,000 in AI networking revenue (2026)

quarterly_data.signal: 800G ADOPTION, 1.6T NEXT: EOS-based products are deployed across 10 gig to 800 gigabit Ethernet speeds with '1.6 terabit migration imminent'; 'an excellent uptick in 800 gig adoption in 2025, gaining greater than 100 customers cumulatively for our Etherlink products'; Arista is 'co-designing several AI rack systems with 1.6 switching emerging this year'. Arista surpassed 150,000,000 cumulative ports shipped in Q4 2025. The EtherLink AI portfolio (three families of spine-leaf fabric) is deployed in scale up, scale out and scale across networks; in 2025 Arista was a founding member of ESUN (Ethernet for scale-up) and completed the Ultra Ethernet Consortium 1.0 specification for scale-out.
quarterly_data.figure: greater than 100 customers cumulatively (800 gig); 1.6 terabit migration imminent; 150,000,000 cumulative ports

quarterly_data.signal: FOUR LARGE AI CUSTOMERS: CEO Jayshree Ullal said Arista is in all four customers deploying AI with Ethernet. 'Three of them have already deployed a cumulative of 100,000 GPUs' and are migrating beyond pilots into production at other centers, with 'power being the biggest constraint'. The fourth 'is migrating from InfiniBand', is still below 100,000 GPUs, and she fully expects it to get there this year.
quarterly_data.figure: Three of them have already deployed a cumulative of 100,000 GPUs; fourth still below 100,000 GPUs

quarterly_data.signal: ACCELERATOR MIX SHIFT: CEO Jayshree Ullal said a year ago Arista's AI deployments were 'pretty much 99% NVIDIA'; today 'we see about 20%, maybe a little more, 20 to 25%, where AMD is becoming the preferred accelerator of choice', and in those multivendor open configurations 'Arista is clearly preferred' because customers build best-of-breed blocks for the NIC, network and I/O and want open standards rather than a full vertical stack from one vendor. Model builders are no longer in one data center but spread across multiple colos, locations and partnerships with cloud titans, which Arista expects to serve both as AI specialty providers and through its cloud titan customers.
quarterly_data.figure: 99% NVIDIA a year ago; 20 to 25% AMD today

quarterly_data.signal: DEFERRED REVENUE FROM AI ACCEPTANCE: total deferred revenue $5,400,000,000, up from $4,700,000,000 in the prior quarter, mostly product-related; product deferred revenue up approximately $469,000,000 as new products, new customers and AI use cases carry customer-specific acceptance clauses. CFO Chantelle Breithaupt: 'The acceptance criteria for that for the larger deployments is 12 to 18 months', some as short as six months; releases can feel lumpy and she does not guide deferred.
quarterly_data.figure: $5,400,000,000, up from $4,700,000,000; product deferred revenue increased approximately $469,000,000; 12 to 18 months

players.product: EtherLink AI switches + XPO (extended pluggable optics) form factor

quarterly_data.signal: SCALE-ACROSS / DCI AND THE 7800R4: in Q4 2025 Arista launched the flat 7800R4 spine for routing use cases including DCI and AI spine, 'with that massive 460 terabytes of capacity'. CEO Jayshree Ullal: Arista expected its participation to be mostly scale out, but workloads too large for one data center (power, bandwidth, throughput) are being extended across data centers through fiber and very high injection bandwidth DCI routing; Arista is 'pleasantly surprised with the role of coherent long-haul optics, which we do not build', and the companies that build them 'are seeing the lift'. The 7800 spine chassis is the flagship there - 'a full-on Arista flagship box with EOS and all of the virtual output queuing and buffering' - interconnecting regional centers as a 'universal AI spine'.

SCALE-UP TIMING (point-in-time; later calls pushed revenue out): CEO Jayshree Ullal said today's configurations are mostly a combination of scale out and scale up on 800 gig and smaller radix. Arista ties its scale-up commitment to new products and the ESUN specification, 'which we expect the earliest to be Q4 this year' - without a solid spec 'we will be shipping proprietary products like some people in the world do today'. Arista will be in trials on active AI racks designed with scale up in mind, 'But the real production level will be in 2027. Primarily centered around not just 800 gig, but 1.6T.'
quarterly_data.figure: ESUN spec earliest to be Q4 this year; real production level will be in 2027
